brief: A drone workbench station: a flat covered working top with a bin beside it for screws. Dress it for a build session: a 5 inch quad on the top, a hex driver set and a LiPo battery nearby.

requirements.evidence: Three full bases (0,0), (0,1) and (1,0) in a triangle, each with a solid top cover. Together they make a flat surface at 80 mm, but it is made of three separate cover panels, not one continuous sheet.

requirements.requirement: Bin beside the top for screws
requirements.evidence: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 is a full-depth bin with 3 compartments in base (-1,0), next to the top and bolted to it. An M3 screws prop sits in the middle compartment.

requirements.requirement: Station holds together as one unit
requirements.evidence: Joint bolts on the three walls jointBolt:0#-1,0#0, 0#0,0#0 and 0#0,0#5. The configurator said the (0,1)–(1,0) wall was already bolted. check_build shows no loose-body warning.
The quad-5in prop rests on the cover of base (1,0). It was refused at the centre of the top because it would overlap the bin wall.
The hexdriver-set prop is on the cover of base (0,1), beside the quad.
A lipo-4s prop is on the cover of base (0,0), beside the quad.

finish.summary: I built a drone workbench from 11 parts: four bases, three solid top covers making the working top, a full-depth 3-compartment screw bin to its left, and three joint bolts. Props for a build session are placed: the 5 inch quad on the top, the hex driver set and a 4S LiPo beside it, and M3 screws in the bin. check_build shows no rule errors and the mesh-collision check is clear. The only note is that 16 open faces could take caps. Props are staging only and are not in the parts list.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
